Backends.fromDeploy: These settings came with the deploy. Changing any of them here takes over from it.
Backends.pcoDescription: Where Tally reads your people from. It keeps no copy of them.
Backends.pcoAskFailed: Could not ask Tally about the connection.
Backends.pcoRefreshed: Read the roster again from Planning Center
Backends.pcoRefreshFailed: Could not refresh from Planning Center.
Backends.pcoWriteOff: Tally never writes to Planning Center. Visitors stay queued until this is turned on.
Backends.pcoWriteCreate: Tally creates people it has not seen before, but never edits an existing one.
Backends.pcoWriteFull: Tally creates people, and Edit profile saves a linked student’s name, grade and allergies straight to Planning Center. It can also add an adult — creating the household if there is none — and put a phone number or email on them.
Backends.pcoCacheOff: Caching is off. Every screen asks Planning Center directly — slower, and always current.
Backends.pcoCacheOn: An answer is reused for up to {count, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} before Tally asks Planning Center again.
Backends.pcoRosterNote: Who is on the roster is Tally's own list — add and remove students on the Students screen. Planning Center supplies their names, grades and parent contact, and Tally stores none of it.
Backends.pcoUnresolved: {count, plural, one {# student is} other {# students are}} on the roster but can no longer be read from Planning Center — deleted or merged upstream.
Backends.pcoQueuedWriteOff: {count, plural, one {# student has} other {# students have}} no Planning Center person yet — and none will be created while write-back is off.
Backends.pcoQueued: {count, plural, one {# student has} other {# students have}} no Planning Center person yet. Push them from the Queued badge on their roster row.
Backends.pcoRosterOffline: This device is showing a roster it saved earlier. Check-in still works; anyone added since will not appear until Planning Center is reachable again.
Backends.secretManagerNote: The credentials themselves live in Secret Manager and are not editable from the app.
Backends.a32Description: A second place Tally can read people from, beside Planning Center.
Backends.a32AskFailed: Could not ask Tally about the connections.
Backends.a32Refreshed: Read the roster again from every connected backend
Backends.a32WriteOff: Tally never writes to Attendees. Visitors stay queued until this is turned on.
Backends.a32WriteCreate: Tally creates attendees it has not seen before, but never edits an existing one.
Backends.a32WriteFull: Tally creates attendees, and Edit profile saves a linked student’s name, grade, allergies and birthday straight to Attendees. It can also add an adult to the family and fill in their phone or email.
Backends.a32RosterNote: Students added from Attendees keep their Attendees record as the source of their name, grade and family — exactly as Planning Center students do theirs.
Backends.a32Unresolved: {count, plural, one {# student is} other {# students are}} on the roster but can no longer be read from Attendees — removed upstream.
Backends.a32NothingConnected: Nothing is connected yet. Run the setup command on your Attendees server, put its token in Secret Manager, then enter the addresses and slugs it prints under Change.
Backends.tokenNote: The token itself lives in Secret Manager and is not editable from the app.
Backends.newStudentsDescription: Which system a student created in Tally — a quick-add at the door — is pushed to.
Backends.defaultChangeFailed: Could not change where new students go.
Backends.queuedGoingTo: {count, plural, one {# student is} other {# students are}} queued and will go to {backend} on the next push.
Backends.notMoved: Students already linked to a backend are not moved by this — it decides only where a brand-new student's record is created.
Backends.heldForReview: {count, plural, one {# student registered themselves at the kiosk and is waiting for somebody to approve them.} other {# students registered themselves at the kiosk and are waiting for somebody to approve them.}}
Backends.gradeRangeError: Cannot end below where it starts.
Backends.pcoGradeBandNote: Who is on the roster is decided on the Students screen, one student at a time. This band only says where a student Planning Center has no grade for lands, and it is the range the app understands at all.
Backends.pcoWriteHintOff: Tally never writes to Planning Center. Visitors added at the door stay queued until this is turned on.
Backends.pcoWriteHintCreate: Tally creates people it has not seen before, after searching for a match. It never edits an existing person.
Backends.pcoWriteHintFull: Tally creates people, and Edit profile becomes editable for students Planning Center already has — first name, last name, grade and medical notes are saved there. A leader can also add an adult, and the household if there is none. It offers anybody Planning Center already has by that name before creating a second record, and never overwrites a number on file.
Backends.pcoCacheHintOff: Off. Every screen asks Planning Center directly — slower, and always current.
Backends.pcoCacheHintOn: Eight counselors opening Tally in the same minute cost one read instead of eight. A name corrected in Planning Center appears within {seconds} seconds.
Backends.pcoApiAddressHint: Leave empty to use whatever the deploy configured — currently {url}. Every request carries this church's credentials, so any other address sends them somewhere else: set this only for a proxy you run, or a test rig.
Backends.a32WriteHintOff: Tally never writes to Attendees. Visitors added at the door stay queued until this is turned on.
Backends.a32WriteHintCreate: Tally creates attendees it has not seen before, after searching for a match. It never edits an existing one.
Backends.a32WriteHintFull: Tally creates attendees, and Edit profile becomes editable for students Attendees already has — name, grade, allergies and birthday are saved there. A leader can also add an adult to the family, and fill in their phone or email when Attendees has none.
Backends.a32ConnectedHint: Attendees serves the roster alongside any other connected backend.
Backends.a32DisconnectedHint: Switched off. Students already linked to Attendees stay on the roster but their names cannot be read until this is turned back on.
Backends.a32SlugsNote: Where your students live in Attendees. The setup command on the Attendees side prints all four — they name the division and meet whose attendees are the roster, and the character new students join.
Backends.a32GradeBandNote: The band a student with no grade in Attendees lands in, and the range the app understands at all.
Backends.a32CacheHintOff: Off. Every screen asks Attendees directly — slower, and always current.
Backends.a32CacheHintOn: Eight counselors opening Tally in the same minute cost one read instead of eight. A name corrected in Attendees appears within {seconds} seconds.
Backends.a32ApiAddressHint: Where your Attendees server lives. Every request carries this church's token, so any other address sends it somewhere else — admins only, and only for a server you run.

Team.title: Team
Team.description: Who may sign in to Tally, and what they may do once they have. Changes apply to every phone immediately.
Team.howSummary: How Tally decides who may sign in
Team.howBody: Tally decides access by Google address. An admin invites somebody here, they sign in with that Google account, and their profile appears beside this — from then on the profile decides what they may do. Some admins are pinned by the deployment itself and cannot be changed here; that is the way back in if access is ever lost.
Team.membersDescription: Outstanding invitations are not listed here.
Team.membersEmptyBody: Invite a Google address above, or sign in with one of the addresses named in TALLY_ADMIN_EMAILS.
Team.otherAdminOnly: Another admin has to change this.
Team.invitesDescription: Addresses that may sign in but have not yet.
Team.googleAddressHint: It has to be the Google account they will actually sign in with — Tally matches on the address.
Team.invitesEmptyBody: Everybody who has been invited has signed in.
Team.withdrawWarning: This deletes the invitation for good.

KioskPair.title: Pair a kiosk
KioskPair.intro: On the kiosk device, open <mono>/kiosk</mono>. It shows a six-character code — type it here to sign that kiosk in as you.
KioskPair.whatIsKiosk: <mono>/kiosk</mono> is a self-serve screen for a device in the lobby, served on this same site: families check themselves in by name, or by the last four digits of a household phone number.
KioskPair.retire: To retire a kiosk, clear the browser's site data on the device.
KioskPair.retireCore: To retire a kiosk, clear the browser's site data on the device — or deactivate and reactivate your account to cut every session loose.
KioskPair.blocked: This deployment cannot sign a kiosk in. Approving a code still records it, but the lobby screen keeps waiting until the role below is granted.
KioskPair.codeHint: Codes last ten minutes. If this one is refused, read the code the kiosk is showing now and try again.
KioskPair.outcomeApproved: Approved — the kiosk signs itself in on its next poll, and every check-in it records will be under your name.
KioskPair.outcomeNotFound: No kiosk is showing that code. Codes last ten minutes; read the one on the kiosk screen now — the letters I, L, O and the digits 0 and 1 never appear.
KioskPair.outcomeExpired: That code has expired. The kiosk is already showing a fresh one — read it off the screen and try again.
KioskPair.outcomeFailed: Could not reach the server. Try again in a moment.
KioskPair.signingOk: Tally can hand a kiosk a session. It says nothing about the screen in the lobby.
KioskPair.copyFailed: Could not copy — select the command below instead.
KioskPair.stuckPending: Once the role is granted, these are the remaining reasons a kiosk keeps waiting.
KioskPair.stuckHomeScreen: A kiosk installed to the device's home screen keeps its own storage, so it asks to be paired a second time.
KioskPair.stuckDeactivated: A kiosk stops when its approver's access is deactivated. Pair it again from an active account.
KioskPair.phoneSearchNote: Only the last four digits of a household's numbers are ever stored in Tally. The index rebuilds nightly on its own; use this when a family's number changed today.
KioskPair.rebuilt: Phone search rebuilt: {students} students, {entries} number endings.
KioskPair.rebuildFailed: Could not rebuild the kiosk phone index. Is a people backend reachable?
